question: A cement plant receives a bulk cement tanker whose unloading time doubles while receiving-silo pressure remains normal; what evidence can distinguish tanker aeration failure, conveying-line restriction, and receiving-filter resistance before accepting a demurrage or equipment-repair claim?
category: Bulk tanker pneumatic unloading fault attribution
scenario: Slow bulk-cement pneumatic discharge with normal indicated silo pressure
evidence_required: Truck and silo identifiers, product grade, initial/final weights, start-stop timestamps and residual mass
Tanker blower/compressor pressure, air flow or speed, discharge pressure trend and aeration-pad inspection records
Conveying line diameter/routing, elbow inspection, hose condition, blockage history, receiving filter differential pressure and pressure sensor calibration
answer_and_decision_guide: First verify comparable truck load, cement type, route and unload time. Reconcile discharged mass with certified tickets; align blower and line pressure trends with the unloading sequence. A normal single silo pressure indication does not exclude a clogged filter, restricted line or poor tanker fluidization. Use isolation/inspection only under site lockout, depressurization and confined-space rules. Separate evidence of vehicle-side aeration defects from receiving-side restrictions and document uncertainty before assigning demurrage, warranty or repair liability.
source_provenance: Seller-maintained general engineering directory; not a tanker or filter OEM diagnostic manual. Obtain equipment-specific instructions and independent maintenance evidence.
free_first_decision: Use free maintenance records, truck tickets, pressure historian and OEM manuals already held by the plant; do not propose a paid reference unless a specific missing document is demonstrated.

conditional_paid_check.authorization: Verify exact relevant file title, revision, legal use permissions, current price and buyer approval before any paid recommendation; no automatic checkout.

model_limitations: No actual unloading trends, instrument calibration, plant piping drawing or contract demurrage clause provided; cannot diagnose the fault or allocate liability.
